data.text:
This past week, I was honored to attend the 143rd Supreme Convention of the Knights of Columbus in the nation’s capital, Washington, DC, from August 5-7, 2025.  There were 10 Cardinals, 40 Bishops and 90 priests who joined 2,000 Knights and their spouses and families from all over the nation and beyond, including delegations from Canada, Mexico, the Philippines, and Ukraine, to name only few.  From the Province of New Jersey there were three prelates: Cardinal Joseph W. Tobin, https://t.co/bjlnkYfGGW.R. (Newark), Bishop Kurt Burnett (Passaic) and yours truly.  The convention opened on Monday evening with an awards ceremony presided over by Supreme Knight Patrick Kelly and Supreme Chaplain Archbishop William Lori (Baltimore).  Among the honorees was Father Frank Donio, S.A.C., a native of New Jersey, and the Founding Director of the Catholic Apostolate Center and Executive Director of the Conference of Major Superiors of Men, as well as the worthy Chaplain of the District of Columbia Knights. Father Donio received the 2025 International Blessed Michael McGivney Medal, the highest honor given annually to a Knights of Columbus chaplain.  On Tuesday morning, we boarded buses to the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception for the opening celebration of the Eucharist, with the President of the USCCB, Archbishop Timothy Broglio (Archdiocese of Military Services), as celebrant and homilist. At all the liturgies and formal ceremonies, the Fourth Degree Honor Guard of Knights of Columbus led the procession of prelates.  I was delighted to greet bishops who, like myself, were ordained to the episcopacy in 2020: Bishop William Byrne (Springfield), Bishop David Toups (Beaumont ) and Bishop Lou Tylka (Peoria).  Following lunch, Supreme Knight Patrick Kelly gave his report on the Order, and its activities and programs over the past year, encouraging all the Knights to zealously continue works of charity, unity, fraternity and patriotism as “heralds of hope” in every corner of this world. Then the assembled Knights and ladies were treated to an unexpected and most welcome surprise: a video message and blessings from Pope Leo XIV.  That evening there was a formal State Dinner in the convention ballroom, which Cardinal Timothy Dolan (New York) opened with prayer.  Songs were sung from each of the state districts, with Knights waving state flags and singing much of the evening.  The highlight of that dinner was the presentation of the Gaudium et Spes Award to the Honorable Mary Ann Glendon, former Ambassador of the U.S.A. to the Holy See and emerita professor of Law at Harvard University.  On Wednesday morning, we gathered once again to celebrate the Eucharist on the Feast of the Transfiguration in the convention ballroom with Cardinal Joseph W. Tobin, https://t.co/bjlnkYfGGW.R. (Newark) as celebrant and Cardinal Frank Leo (Toronto) as homilist.  That morning there was a business meeting for the Knights and a parallel program for the ladies. The afternoon was open for district gatherings and other activities, including a tour of the St. John Paul II National Shrine. The 60+ Knights and ladies from New Jersey met that evening for supper at Maggiano’s Little Italy in Chevy Chase, for a delicious supper together. Chaplains Father Ernest Rush (Newark) and Father William Smith (Metuchen) joined us for that supper.  On Thursday morning we celebrated a Memorial Mass for all deceased Knights in the convention center ballroom with Supreme Chaplain Archbishop William Lori (Baltimore) as celebrant and homilist.  Following the liturgy, the Knights met for their final business session. Each day of this supreme convention, a chapel was open for Adoration of the Most Blessed Sacrament and private prayer.  Priests were also available daily for the Sacrament of Penance.  On fire with faith, Blessed Michael McGivney founded the Knights of Columbus in 1882 in New Haven, CT, with a mission of charity.  Pope Francis, in his Apostolic Letter that was read at the Mass for Beatification on Oct. 31, 2020, stated that “Blessed Michael McGivney’s zeal for the proclamation of the Gospel and generous concern for the needs of his brothers and sisters made him an outstanding witness of Christian solidarity and fraternal assistance.”  Blessed Michael McGivney, Pray for Us!  Vivat Jesus!
Photo credits: Various Knights of Columbus

China accused the Philippines on Friday of "playing with fire" after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr said the Southeast Asian nation would be drawn into any conflict between China and the United States over Taiwan.

It was responding to remarks by Marcos during a state visit to India that the Philippines' closeness to Taiwan and the large Filipino community there would make involvement necessary in such a conflict.

"'Geographical proximity' and 'large overseas populations' are not excuses for a country to interfere in the internal affairs of others," China's foreign ministry said in a statement.

"We urge the Philippines to earnestly adhere to the one-China principle ... and refrain from playing with fire on issues concerning China's core interests."

Marcos' remarks came amid heightened tension between Beijing and Manila over territorial disputes in the busy waterway of the South China Sea.

Heavy traffic was reported in several parts of Delhi-NCR on Friday as commuters began travelling ahead of the Raksha Bandhan weekend. With the festival coinciding with the weekend, the Delhi Traffic Police has warned of congestion on major highways as large numbers of people are expected to leave the city.

In its advisory, the traffic police cautioned that those heading towards Karnal, Panipat, Sonipat, and Chandigarh via National Highway-44 and the Singhu border may face long delays and should consider taking alternate routes.
